title: fix(objectql, runtime)!: a function's bare-name read is refused naming both when the platform and a package hold the name, and answers nothing for a name only a disabled package holds (ADR-0150 D4)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DDwkEEJd65kqFZGFjQnzBQt)_

Fixes #32907
Fixes #32933
Fixes #32910

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/**` and `content/docs/**` name neither `resolveFunction`/`resolveFunctionEntry` nor `resolvePackageScopedFunction`, and teach no function name held by the platform beside a package or by a disabled package; the prescription ships in the changeset's BREAKING paragraph.

## 维护者速读

1. 改了什么:不带包名按名读函数(`resolveFunction` / `resolveFunctionEntry`,以及无调用包的 `resolvePackageScopedFunction`)时,平台(无主注册)与一个包同持一个名字,一律 409 点名双方,不再按注册先后答其一;只有已停用包持有的名字不再答该包的函数(停用包仍计为持有者,照样参与歧义判定)。运行时重绑从持有者集读回保留函数,不再走裸读。另补 #32910 的四组运行时钉子。
2. 为什么改:ADR-0150 D4 规定无包调用方在平台+包同名时应被拒并点名双方,原实现只数包,按先后答或答空;ruling A(6824698376)要求停用包"计为持有者、永不被解析到"。
3. 风险与回滚:只收窄(Clause-② no (narrowing),标题带 `!`),原先被拒的一律仍拒,无任何放宽;仍会答的:单一启用包、仅平台、调用方自身包。第一方:仓内无平台与包同名的函数注册(见 Acceptance notes)。回滚即还原本 PR。
4. 先看:`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts` 的 `callerlessFunctionResolution`;`packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts` 的 `bareFunctionEntry`;`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` 的 `releaseMovedFunctions` 中 `bare:` 一行。
5. 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-request-family.test.ts`,预期 78/78 绿;其中 `[#32907]`、`[#32933]` 两组在 main 上 5 条红。
6. 需要你做的:裁定 #32933 的读法(见 Acceptance notes 的 needs_decision:本 PR 实施"计数不解析",另一读法"只数在用持有者"会放宽两个格子)。

## What changes

The engine keeps every holder of a function name: each package that registered one, and the platform for a registration under no package (`ObjectQL#functionHoldersOf`). A read that names no package resolves the name by ADR-0150 D3 over those holders.

1. **#32907 — the platform beside a package is two holders.** `bareFunctionEntry` (`packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts`, the body of `ObjectQL#resolveFunction` / `resolveFunctionEntry`) now always runs the rule (`resolvePackageScopedHolders`, caller with no package) over the holder set, platform included. Before, it consulted the rule only when two PACKAGES held the name, and otherwise answered the bare map's last registration, so the platform plus one package answered by order (the package's entry, or the platform's when it registered last) or nothing after a third, last-registered package left. Now every one of those cells is `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, reason `ambiguous-in-environment`, candidates `[package, platform]` — the same refusal the caller-less `resolvePackageScopedFunction` already answered, so the two reads agree. When the rule resolves (one holder), the answer is still the bare map's entry, the same entry object, so the one-holder answer is unchanged byte for byte. PR #32877's CONTROL pin for this row is flipped to the verdict.
2. **#32933 — a disabled package is counted, never resolved to.** New `callerlessFunctionResolution` (`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts`, not re-exported from the package entry) post-filters the rule's answer for a caller with no package: when the rule picked a package as the environment's unique holder (`via: 'unique-holder'`, the step only a caller with no package reaches) and the registry says that package is disabled (`SchemaRegistry#isPackageDisabled`), the answer is `not-found`. Both the bare read and `resolvePackageScopedFunction` apply it. Refusals are computed over EVERY holder, the disabled one included, so a disable never turns a refused name into an answer. A caller naming its own package, a caller's closure step, the platform's item and every refusal pass through unchanged. The every-holder doors (the hook binder's bind after the seal, `claimBareNameFunctions`; the cold-boot seal, `sealBareNameHolders`) read the registry's claims, which never looked at enablement; they are pinned, not changed.
3. **Runtime re-bind — read the kept entry off the holder set.** `releaseMovedFunctions` (`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`) read the bare slot of each kept name through `resolveFunctionEntry`. With (1) that read throws for a name the platform holds beside the package — aborting the re-bind's teardown — and with (2) it answers nothing for a disabled package, which would drop the owner spelling the package held a kept function by. For a name the package alone holds the bare slot IS the package's holder entry (one entry object in both maps), so the binder now uses that entry; the two-package case (`packageHolders.length > 1`) is unchanged.
4. **#32910 — runtime pins only** (no code): the re-bind before the seal (N4), the move path's ordering CONTROL (D2-N1), the other owner-spelling order (D2-N2).

No `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` symbol is changed (`registry_symbols`: none). No export is added; `engine.ts` changes docblocks only.

## Tests

Pins, numbered for this PR (no numeral lives in the files; the skipped (iii) of #32910's "Numbering" item was in PR #32877's body only, so there is nothing to renumber in the file):

- objectql `src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-request-family.test.ts`
  - (i) flipped: `[#32534] … the platform and one package remain after the last-registered package leaves … (FROM nothing TO 409)` — was the CONTROL "current behaviour, see #32907".
  - (ii) `[#32907] … the package registered last (FROM the package's entry TO 409)`.
  - (iii) `[#32907] … the platform registered last (FROM the platform's entry TO 409)` — the platform-last-registrant cell.
  - (iv) `[#32933] a name only a disabled package holds: the bare read and the caller-less read answer nothing; enabled again, both answer it`.
  - (v) `[#32933] counted: the platform beside a disabled package is still two holders`.
  - CONTROLs: the platform alone and one package alone answer; a caller package holding the name resolves its own beside the platform; the disabled package's own read resolves its own; two packages, one disabled, stay refused naming both; after the seal a co-owner's bind of a name a disabled package holds is refused naming it; the cold-boot seal reports a co-owner clash with one holder disabled.
- runtime `src/app-artifact-handlers.test.ts`
  - (vi) the teardown it.each gains a row: the platform holds the name beta keeps too — the teardown runs whole, the bare read is refused `[beta, platform]`.
  - (vii) N4, it.each moved / dropped: a re-bind before the seal releases the old owner's claim; the seal then reports no clash.
  - (viii) D2-N1 CONTROL: the move path releases after the old owner's kept functions are registered again — a function the new bind neither moves nor gives back keeps its claim.
  - (ix) D2-N2, it.each moved / dropped: the bare-id registration before the bind; the removal takes the entry the bind replaced it with and the claim is released.
  - (x) CONTROL: a disabled old owner keeps a kept function under the bare-id spelling it held it by, and its claim.

The red-on-main reading and the ablations ran before the merge (the reading on `90423f6b`, every ablation on `e8106eb3`); the merge touched none of the files they read.

Red on main / green after: (i)–(v) are red on `main`'s objectql sources and green on this head; every objectql CONTROL is green on both. (vi)–(x) pin behaviour `main` already has (the #32910 rows are coverage of #32534's release; (vi) and (x) guard the re-bind against this PR's engine change), so each is proven by its ablation instead.

## Acceptance notes

- **needs_decision — #32933's reading.** #32933 asks the bare and caller-less function reads to "answer from served holders only" (#32497's default). #32907's own constraint says "Ruling A 6824698376: a disabled package is still a holder" and "anything refused today stays refused", and ruling A says a disabled holder is "counted, never resolved to". The two readings agree on a name only a disabled package holds (nothing answers — implemented) and disagree on two cells: (a) two packages, one disabled; (b) the platform beside a disabled package. Served-only answers the enabled holder / the platform there, where today both are refused (409): a loosening. Per the dispatch's red line this PR implements the reading that never loosens — counted, never resolved to — and pins both cells refused. Alternative: served-only (drop disabled packages from `packageHolders` for these reads, keep the caller's own); cost one filter plus two pins flipped, and an explicit epic ruling that a disable may turn a refusal into an answer for functions.
- **#32910 D2-N2 wording.** "still holds under another owner spelling" ships in the released `packages/objectql/CHANGELOG.md` and `packages/runtime/CHANGELOG.md` entries of PR #32877; qualifying it "in the engine's holder set" is a release-owned file, so it is owed as a dedicated docs-only PR, never this one.
- **First-party exposure: 0 measured by source scan.** Outside tests, no first-party code registers an owner-less engine function: `ObjectQL#registerFunction` has one non-test caller, the hook binder, which passes the bind's `packageId`, and every first-party bind of functions is the app-artifact binder's, under `app:` plus the package id (the objectql plugin's `metadata-service` binds carry hooks, no functions). So no first-party name is held by the platform beside a package. A disabled package's function is reached by a caller-less read only when an environment-authored flow names it.
